title: Patient Financial Services Policy: Changing the Billing Method on a Laboratory Test Order
content:
## Insurance to self-pay

An insurance-billed Laboratory Test Orders order may be switched to self-pay only while no claim has been submitted for it. There must be no claim-submitted line for the order in the claims record kept under Insurance Coverage & Claims. The switch to self-pay must also be made no later than the class's insurance-to-self-pay window, in calendar days after the collection date on the order.

A switch to self-pay is the patient's election to pay the self-pay price of every test in full and to have the order withheld from the health plan. When the class requires self-pay payment at collection, payment is due at collection.

## Self-pay to insurance

A self-pay order may be switched to insurance only when the coverage named for the switch is active, its effective date is on or before the collection date, and it has no termination date before that date. The switch must also be made no later than the class's self-pay-to-insurance window, in calendar days after the collection date on the order. When the class requires prior authorization for that coverage's payer class, the switched order also needs an approved authorization before testing.

## How both windows are counted

Both windows count calendar days with the collection date as day 0, the last day included. For an order not yet collected, the switch is open without a time limit.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical 10-day window, collection on 3 May).**

| Switch made on | Day | Within the window |
|---|---|---|
| 13 May | 10 | Yes |
| 14 May | 11 | No |
| Any date, specimen not yet collected | — | Yes, no time limit |

**Coverage test for a switch to insurance (hypothetical collection on 3 May).**

| Coverage status | Effective date | Termination date | Switch to insurance allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active | 1 January | none | Yes |
| Active | 10 May | none | No (effective after the collection date) |
| Active | 1 January | 30 April | No (terminated before the collection date) |
| Not active | 1 January | none | No |

## Client billing

Client billing is elected only by the ordering practice, never by the patient, and only where the intake rule allows it.
